result.title: On Adaptive Step Sizes for Eligibility Traces in Deep Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Many deep reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms store agent-environment interactions in a replay buffer and later learn by sampling transitions from it. However, this approach can be memory-inefficient and can delay learning because the agent can learn from a transition only when the buffer samples it. Additionally, most of these methods use one-step or short multi-step temporal-difference (TD) updates, which are slow at credit assignment. An alternative approach is to learn from the stream of observations as they arrive without relying on a buffer. Eligibility-trace algorithms allow these incremental updates and can also assign credit over many steps. These algorithms were common with linear function approximation but have only recently been used in deep RL. Basic questions, such as how to use vector step sizes with eligibility traces in the deep RL setting, remain open. In this work, we first show that adaptive vector step sizes must be part of the eligibility trace to keep the equivalence between the forward and backward views. We then show that the step sizes of common optimizers, such as Adam, do not have an online backward view. We introduce a new optimizer, Function-Space Distance (FSD), that maintains the forward-backward equivalence. We test four eligibility-trace algorithms covering semi-gradient and gradient TD updates, as well as value-based and actor-critic methods. We show that FSD performs better than SGD or naively applied Adam. The resulting algorithms outperform or match other streaming methods and are comparable to or better than PPO, which uses a buffer, in most environments. Code available at https://github.com/esraaelelimy/ada_traces

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究 deep RL 中 eligibility trace 的向量步长问题，论证自适应向量步长必须纳入 trace 才能保持 forward/backward 视角等价，指出 Adam 等优化器缺少在线 backward view，并提出 Function-Space Distance（FSD）优化器，在四类 trace 算法上验证其优于 SGD 与直接套用的 Adam。
AI.relevance_reason: 其无需 replay buffer 的多步增量贡献分配机制及「保持前后向等价」的步长设计，可能为 latent 推理轨迹上的跨步信用分配与训练监督提供线索，但与原论文的视觉多模态场景差异较大，可供核查其可迁移性。
